base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share: median of FY2024 $4.08, FY2025 $3.08, FY2026 $3.79 = $3.79/share (median equals FY2026). FY2026 conservative OE: OCF $2.638B - capex $0.700B - SBC $0.118B = $1.820B on 480.6M diluted shares. No TTM override: FY ended 2026-06-27 (3.5 months ago, not stale) and Q1 FY2027 had not been reported. Standalone Sysco only — Jetro Restaurant Depot (pending, $29.1B EV) excluded from the base and carried only in the super-bull scenario.
moat_justification: Scale cost advantage as the largest US foodservice distributor (~17% share vs US Foods ~10%): purchasing terms, 333-center route density, Sysco Brand private label, 50+ years of dividend growth and historically double-digit ROIC (Morningstar: narrow moat) — against low customer switching costs and multi-sourcing, locally fragmented competition from 15,000 distributors plus scaled USFD/PFG, decade-flat ~18-19% gross margins (limited pricing power), labor/fuel intensity, and structural share loss of price-sensitive independents to cash-and-carry (the gap the $29.1B Jetro deal is buying into).
name: Sysco Corporation
one_liner: Durable scale distributor, moat 6/10, with clean owner's earnings ($3.79/share, both definitions agree) — but at $78.26 (20.7x OE, 4.8% yield) it yields an 8.2% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $34.64, and even the Jetro-success super-bull case (12.3%) stays below the hurdle; it clears 15% only at ~$35 (~$28 with a margin of safety), with ~$11.7B of net debt rising pro forma for the $29.1B Jetro deal as the key risk to watch.
